test: Read chord's pitch thresholds from its variables block and check the ratios

hypothesis: memoryslot 63 (base 0x81be7400) is free arena and the piecewise slot->address law holds
test: Build for slot 63, install through the full-firmware update payload, boot the unit
notes: The engine loads and renders on hardware at that base; no 'Bad address'/'Could not load engine 160' in system.log and the plug plays. The 0x1400-stride law is therefore confirmed by execution, not only by regression over the 14 factory engines in slots 59-89

hypothesis: A new engine can be side-loaded by copying the .engine onto the content disk
test: Place struck.engine at samplepacks/6-lead/08, then repeat with a pristine factory chorus.engine renamed probe.engine as a control
notes: Both refused with 'rejecting invalid engine'. Identical factory bytes and a different name were rejected, so the check is a plug-registry lookup, not a file-validity check: the registry entry (system/content/settings/plugs_patch.json) must exist before the OS will consider the module

hypothesis: A three-entry update zip (engine + plugs_patch.json) passes the updater's validation
test: Stage it as firmware_bin_only_with_bootloader.zip and read systeminfo/upgrade.log
notes: 'failed to find ble firmware file' then 'upgrade not compatible with this device'; the updater validates a complete firmware archive (blackfin bin, nordic bin+dat, psoc cyacd, versions, system/content) before extracting anything

hypothesis: A full firmware tree plus the engine installs the engine as content
test: Repack the unit's own 1.2.45 tree (32 entries, ZIP_STORED, per-entry CRCs) with firmware/blackfin/system/content/engines/struck.engine and a six-entry plugs_patch.json
notes: Accepted and installed; the device wrote ~160.engine markers on all four synth tracks and the engine plays. A zip staged while the unit is in CONTENT mode is silently eaten by the content importer (no upgrade.log entry at all), so it must be staged while the volume shows systeminfo/

hypothesis: A free-free bar ratio set (1, 2.756, 5.404, ...) sounds like a wooden marimba
test: Install on hardware and listen
notes: The engine played correctly and sounded good but glassy, not wooden. The free-free ratios are an untuned bar (glockenspiel/metal); a marimba bar is undercut so its first overtone is tuned to exactly 4x (two octaves)

hypothesis: A marimba is characterised by a tuned 4x first overtone plus per-mode damping that is independent of the note length
test: Measure the rendered spectrum with a single-bin DFT and compare partial levels and decay rates
notes: With MARIMBA ratios (1, 3.93, 9.24, 16, 24, 34) and per-mode radii, the 3.93x partial stands 32.5 dB above the free-free 2.756x partial, and the 9.24x overtone falls 38.7 dB in 150 ms while the fundamental (decay-macro owned) barely moves. Both are now gates in opzverify.py

hypothesis: Factory engines write their audio into their own state block (ctx+8 onward), not into the output buffer argument, so the harness measures the wrong memory
test: For each of the 13 instruments render one block with the corrected ABI, then report the distinct-value count and peak inside ctx+8..ctx+0x134 instead of inside out
notes: State blocks hold only 2-14 distinct values each (sparse state, not 64 frames of audio), so the audio is not parked there

hypothesis: The caller must preset the I registers to the output buffer, as a register-passed out parameter the engines write through instead of the stack argument
test: Set I0 and I1 to the output buffer before each render call and measure the output buffer only
notes: No engine writes to the output buffer even with I0/I1 preset

hypothesis: The 64-frame LSETUP at 0x81be2794 runs its body fewer than 64 times, so chord never produces a full block
test: Count executions of the loop body instruction 0x81be279e during one render and compare against 64
notes: Body runs 65 times (64 frames plus the final pass) and the LSETUP end is visited 65 times, so the loop is correct; chord simply writes each iteration to the same two words at state+8 and never touches the output buffer

hypothesis: Chord reads the output argument as an input buffer and writes its result into state+8, so the OS must be the component that turns an engine's per-tick result into mixed audio
test: Read the OS synth tick (FUN_801184c0) for any read of record+0x50 (state+8) or of the record after the render call
notes: A store census shows chord writing 64 consecutive words into the output buffer (one per frame), so it does write audio there - every value is simply zero)

hypothesis: Chord writes a full block of zeros because its gain path is fed a zero, not because it fails to write audio
test: With the corrected ABI, trace the value chain into the output store at the loop tail and identify the first operand that is zero while on silicon it should not be
notes: The zero came from a decoder bug: Comp3op opcodes 5-7 write POINTER registers (dst = s0+s1, s0+(s1<<1), s0+(s1<<2)) and were being executed as data-register subtracts, so chord's \PtrOp P1 = P2 + (P1 << 2)\" never updated P1 and its wavetable load used the bare index 0x37 as an address")
